payload.text: PATH on rhadamanth: hv uses the brew release of every tool unless a project is being worked on, and runs `utilz use brew` himself (hv's ruling via molt-vc, through vc, 25 Oct). So a bare utilz may be brew's release, not the primary's dev links (Molt-matts a258ad0 put ~/.local/bin first). Every dc run on the Mac, the twins and the dry run among them, names its own tree's bin/ (eg <tree>/bin/utilz), never a plain utilz from PATH, and logs `command -v utilz` and `utilz --version`. kovacs runs put the run tree's bin/ first on PATH and check every name resolves into it. A release's checklist ends with brew upgraded on both hosts, `utilz use brew`, and `utilz --version` showing (brew, <release sha>) from a fresh login shell.
